questions.q: Which network type typically uses Bluetooth or Zigbee as its primary communication technology and covers a radius of about 10 metres around a person?
questions.a: PAN (Personal Area Network). A wrong answer (e.g., LAN) reveals the student confuses short-range personal device communication with building-scale networks; they likely memorised acronyms without associating each with its characteristic technology and distance.

questions.q: A company has offices in three buildings within a 2 km radius. They lay their own fibre-optic cables to interconnect the buildings. Is this a LAN or a MAN? Explain why the ownership of the medium matters for classification.
questions.a: It is a LAN because the geographical span (2 km) falls within the LAN range (typically up to a few km) and the organisation owns the entire infrastructure. A wrong answer (MAN) shows the student thinks any multi-building network is a MAN, ignoring that MANs usually span a city (5–50 km) and often lease circuits from telecom providers.

questions.q: A city government deploys a wireless network covering 40 km to connect traffic cameras, smart streetlights, and municipal offices. They use a mix of licensed microwave links and fibre leased from a telecom operator. Classify this network and justify your answer with two distinguishing features of that class.
questions.a: MAN (Metropolitan Area Network). Features: (1) geographical span of a city (5–50 km), (2) typically uses a combination of owned and leased media (microwave, leased fibre). A wrong answer (WAN) indicates the student overestimates the distance threshold for WAN or misses that WANs cross national/regional boundaries using public switched networks.

questions.q: Compare the typical latency and bandwidth characteristics of a LAN (1 Gbps Ethernet) and a WAN (leased line 100 Mbps) when transferring a 10 GB dataset between two endpoints. Which will complete faster and why?
questions.a: LAN will complete faster. Latency on LAN is sub-millisecond; on WAN it is tens of milliseconds. Bandwidth is higher on LAN (1 Gbps vs 100 Mbps). Transfer time ≈ size/bandwidth + latency overhead. For 10 GB: LAN ≈ 80 seconds; WAN ≈ 800 seconds. A wrong answer (WAN faster) reveals confusion between bandwidth and latency or ignorance of the huge latency penalty in WANs.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "A PAN is just a very small LAN, so the same security policies (firewalls, VLANs) apply." Defend or refute with two technical reasons.
questions.a: Refute. (1) PANs use ad-hoc, low-power protocols (Bluetooth, Zigbee) that do not support IP-based firewalls or VLAN tagging. (2) PAN devices often lack an OS capable of running enterprise security agents; they rely on pairing encryption and proximity. A wrong answer (agree) shows the student overlooks protocol-stack differences and device capabilities.

questions.q: Design a network plan for a multinational bank headquartered in Mumbai with branches in Delhi, London, and Singapore. Specify the network type for each link (HQ↔branch, branch↔ATMs, teller↔cash-recycler) and the primary technology you would choose for each. Justify each choice in one sentence.
questions.a: HQ↔branch: WAN (MPLS/VPN over internet) – connects across countries. Branch↔ATMs: MAN (metro Ethernet/fibre) – spans city. Teller↔cash-recycler: PAN (USB/Bluetooth) – <1 m personal device link. A poor answer uses LAN for HQ↔Delhi (ignores national boundary) or WAN for teller↔cash-recycler (overkill, wrong scale).

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A computer network is classified by its geographical span into four primary types: Personal Area Network (PAN) covers a few metres around an individual (e.g., Bluetooth); Local Area Network (LAN) spans a single building or campus up to a few kilometres; Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) extends across a city (5–50 km); Wide Area Network (WAN) connects networks across countries or continents using public ______ infrastructure.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you are designing the network ______ for a new university.

Fill in the blank: The campus has multiple buildings (LAN), the university wants to connect its city campus to a suburban research park ______ km away (MAN), and it also needs to link to its international partner campuses (WAN).
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Given a real-world scenario (e.g., "a school campus", "a smartwatch syncing with a phone", "a bank connecting branches across India", "a city-wide Wi-Fi project"), the student must correctly identify the network type (PAN/LAN/MAN/WAN), justify the choice using geographical scope and typical technology, and state one advantage and one.
